jp-20261028-news-1.title: What is the "Training and Employment" System Starting in April 2027? Changes from Technical Intern Training and Preparations Required for Companies and Foreign Talent

segments.src: ## 開始まで半年、制度の全体像を確認する
segments.tr: ## Six months until the start: Checking the overall picture of the system

segments.src: 2027年4月に始まる予定の「育成就労」制度は、長く続いてきた技能実習制度に代わる新しい在留の仕組みです。2024年6月に関連する法律が成立し、2027年までに施行される旨が定められました。開始まで約半年となった今、受け入れを検討する企業や自治体、そして日本で働くことを考える外国人にとって、何が変わり何が変わらないのかを整理しておくことが大切です。
segments.tr: The "Training and Employment" system, scheduled to begin in April 2027, is a new residency framework that will replace the long-standing Technical Intern Training Program. Relevant laws were enacted in June 2024, stipulating that the system will be implemented by 2027. With about six months left until the start, it is important for companies and local governments considering accepting foreign workers, as well as for foreigners thinking about working in Japan, to organize what will change and what will remain the same.

segments.src: なお、制度の詳細は省令や基本方針、分野別の運用方針などで順次具体化されています。実際の手続きに進む際は、出入国在留管理庁や厚生労働省、各分野の所管省庁が公表する最新の情報を必ず確認してください。
segments.tr: Please note that the details of the system are being concretized sequentially through ministerial ordinances, basic policies, and operational policies by sector. When proceeding with actual procedures, please be sure to check the latest information published by the Immigration Services Agency of Japan, the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare, and the competent ministries for each sector.

segments.src: ## 技能実習と育成就労、目的の違い
segments.tr: ## Differences in purpose: Technical Intern Training vs. Training and Employment

segments.src: 技能実習制度は「国際貢献」を目的に、技能を母国へ移転することを建前としてきました。一方で、実態としては国内の人手不足を補う労働力として機能してきたため、目的と運用のずれが以前から指摘されてきました。
segments.tr: The Technical Intern Training Program has ostensibly aimed for "international contribution" by transferring skills to the home country. However, since it has functioned in reality as a labor force to compensate for domestic labor shortages, the discrepancy between its purpose and operation has been pointed out for some time.

segments.src: 育成就労制度は、この点を見直し、**人材の育成と確保**を目的として明確にしています。原則3年の就労を通じて、特定技能1号の水準の技能を身につけてもらうことが想定されています。つまり、入口の育成就労から、特定技能へ、さらに長期的な就労へとつながる道筋を示す制度設計です。
segments.tr: The Training and Employment system reviews this point and clearly defines its purpose as the **development and securing of human resources**. It is envisioned that through principle three years of employment, workers will acquire skills at the level of Specified Skilled Worker (i). In other words, it is a system design that shows a path from the entry point of Training and Employment to Specified Skilled Worker, and further to long-term employment.

segments.src: ## 主な変更点
### 1. 転籍（職場の変更）が一定の条件で可能に
segments.tr: ### 1. Job transfers (changing workplaces) will be possible under certain conditions

segments.src: 技能実習では、原則として実習先の変更（転籍）が認められず、人間関係や労働環境に問題があっても動きにくいことが課題とされました。育成就労では、やむを得ない事情がある場合の転籍に加え、次のような条件を満たせば**本人の意向による転籍**も認められる方向です。
segments.tr: Under the Technical Intern Training Program, changing the training site (transfer) was generally not permitted, which was considered an issue as it made it difficult for interns to move even if there were problems with interpersonal relationships or working conditions. Under the Training and Employment system, in addition to transfers due to unavoidable circumstances, **transfers based on the individual's own intention** are also expected to be permitted if the following conditions are met:

segments.src: - 同じ業務区分の中での転籍であること
segments.tr: - The transfer must be within the same job category

segments.src: - 一定期間以上の就労を経ていること（分野ごとに1年から2年の範囲で設定される見込み）
segments.tr: - The individual must have worked for a certain period or longer (expected to be set between 1 and 2 years depending on the sector)

segments.src: - 一定水準の技能と日本語能力の試験に合格していること
segments.tr: - The individual must have passed a certain level of skill and Japanese language proficiency tests

segments.src: - 転籍先が適正な受け入れ体制を備えていること
segments.tr: - The new workplace must have an appropriate acceptance system in place

segments.src: 企業にとっては、人材が他社へ移る可能性が制度上あることを意味します。賃金水準、職場環境、教育体制といった「選ばれる職場づくり」がこれまで以上に重要になります。
segments.tr: For companies, this means that there is a possibility under the system that talent may move to other companies. Creating a "workplace of choice" in terms of wage levels, work environment, and educational systems will become more important than ever.

segments.src: ### 2. 受け入れ分野は特定技能と整合的に
segments.tr: ### 2. Acceptance sectors to be consistent with Specified Skilled Worker

segments.src: 育成就労の対象分野は、原則として特定技能制度の分野と対応させる形で設定されます。技能実習にあった職種のすべてがそのまま引き継がれるわけではなく、分野によっては対象外になる業務も出てきます。自社の業務がどの分野・業務区分に該当するのかを、早めに確認しておきましょう。
segments.tr: The sectors covered by Training and Employment will, in principle, be set to correspond with the sectors of the Specified Skilled Worker system. Not all job types that existed under the Technical Intern Training Program will be carried over as they are, and some tasks may become ineligible depending on the sector. Be sure to check early on which sector and job category your company's operations fall under.

segments.src: ### 3. 分野ごとの受け入れ上限
国は、人手不足の状況などを踏まえ、分野ごとに受け入れ見込数の上限を設ける方針です。上限は経済情勢や産業の需給を見ながら見直されます。希望する人数を必ず受け入れられるとは限らないため、採用計画は制度の運用状況を見ながら柔軟に立てる必要があります。
segments.tr: The government plans to set caps on the number of people expected to be accepted for each sector, taking into account the labor shortage situation. The caps will be reviewed while watching economic conditions and industrial supply and demand. Since it is not guaranteed that you will be able to accept the number of people you desire, recruitment plans need to be made flexibly while monitoring the operation of the system.

segments.src: ### 4. 日本語能力の要件
就労開始前の段階で、日本語の基礎的な能力（目安として日本語能力試験N5相当など）が求められる見通しです。その後、特定技能1号への移行時にはより高い水準が求められます。企業側にも、入国後の日本語学習の機会を確保することが期待されます。
segments.tr: It is expected that basic Japanese language proficiency (as a guideline, equivalent to JLPT N5, etc.) will be required before starting employment. Subsequently, a higher level will be required when transitioning to Specified Skilled Worker (i). Companies are also expected to ensure opportunities for Japanese language learning after arrival in Japan.

segments.src: ### 5. 監理・支援体制の見直し
segments.tr: ### 5. Review of supervision and support systems

segments.src: 技能実習の監理団体は、育成就労では「監理支援機関」へと位置づけが改められます。許可要件が厳しくなり、受け入れ企業との利害関係が強い団体は適切な監理が行えないよう、外部監視の強化なども盛り込まれています。技能実習の実施状況を監督してきた外国人技能実習機構も、「外国人育成就労機構」へと改組される予定です。
segments.tr: The supervisory organizations for Technical Intern Training will be repositioned as "supervisory support organizations" under Training and Employment. Permission requirements will become stricter, and measures such as strengthening external monitoring are included to prevent organizations with strong conflicts of interest with accepting companies from conducting appropriate supervision. The Organization for Technical Intern Training, which has supervised the implementation of technical intern training, is also scheduled to be reorganized into the "Organization for Training and Employment of Foreign Workers."

segments.src: ### 6. 悪質な仲介業者への対応
来日前に外国人が高額な手数料を負担し、借金を抱える問題が指摘されてきました。育成就労では、二国間取決めを通じて送出機関を適正なものに絞り込み、手数料の負担のあり方も見直す方針です。受け入れ企業が費用の一部を負担する仕組みも想定されており、コスト構造は従来と変わる可能性があります。
segments.tr: The problem of foreigners bearing high fees before coming to Japan and falling into debt has been pointed out. Under Training and Employment, the policy is to narrow down sending organizations to appropriate ones through bilateral agreements and to review how fees are borne. A mechanism where the accepting company bears part of the costs is also envisioned, and the cost structure may change from the conventional one.

segments.src: ## 企業・自治体が今から確認したいこと
segments.tr: ## What companies and local governments should check now

segments.src: 1. **自社の業務が対象分野に含まれるか**：分野・業務区分を確認します。
segments.tr: 1. **Does your company's work fall under the target sectors?**: Check the sector and job category.

segments.src: 2. **現在の技能実習生の扱い**：施行日前に受け入れた実習生は、経過措置のもとで技能実習を継続できる見通しです。移行の時期や方法を整理しておきます。
segments.tr: 2. **Handling of current technical interns**: Interns accepted before the enforcement date are expected to be able to continue their technical intern training under transitional measures. Organize the timing and method of transition.

segments.src: 3. **受け入れ体制の整備**：指導担当者の配置、教育計画、住居や生活支援、相談窓口の整備が必要です。
segments.tr: 3. **Development of acceptance system**: It is necessary to arrange instructors, educational plans, housing, life support, and consultation counters.

segments.src: 4. **賃金・処遇の見直し**：転籍が可能になることを前提に、同じ地域・同じ業種の水準と比べて見劣りしないかを点検します。
segments.tr: 4. **Review of wages and treatment**: On the premise that transfers will become possible, check whether they are inferior compared to the standards of the same region and the same industry.

segments.src: 5. **日本語学習の支援**：学習時間の確保や教材、地域の日本語教室との連携を検討します。
segments.tr: 5. **Support for Japanese language learning**: Consider securing study time, teaching materials, and cooperation with local Japanese language classes.

segments.src: 6. **監理支援機関の選定**：許可を受けた機関かどうか、支援内容や費用を比較して選びます。
segments.tr: 6. **Selection of supervisory support organization**: Choose by comparing support content and costs, and whether it is an authorized organization.

segments.src: 7. **自治体の役割**：転籍により、都市部への人材流出が起こる可能性も議論されています。地域に定着してもらうための生活環境や情報提供が課題になります。
segments.tr: 7. **Role of local governments**: There is also discussion about the possibility of talent outflow to urban areas due to transfers. Providing living environments and information to help them settle in the region will be a challenge.

segments.src: ## 外国人材にとってのポイント
育成就労は、キャリアの見通しを立てやすい制度でもあります。技能と日本語を段階的に身につけ、特定技能1号、さらに2号へと進めば、在留期間の更新に上限がなくなり、家族の帯同が認められる道も開けます。
segments.tr: Training and Employment is also a system that makes it easier to plan your career. If you acquire skills and Japanese language step by step and advance to Specified Skilled Worker (i) and then to (ii), there will be no upper limit on the renewal of your period of stay, and a path to bringing your family will also open up.

segments.src: 一方で、転籍には条件があり、自由に職場を移れるわけではありません。契約内容や賃金、手数料、就労条件を事前によく確認し、困ったときに相談できる公的な窓口（外国人技能実習機構・育成就労機構や、地方の労働基準監督署、外国人向け相談センターなど）を知っておくことが重要です。
segments.tr: On the other hand, there are conditions for transfers, and you cannot freely change workplaces. It is important to carefully check contract details, wages, fees, and working conditions in advance, and to know public consultation counters (such as the Organization for Technical Intern Training/Organization for Training and Employment, local Labor Standards Inspection Offices, and consultation centers for foreigners) where you can consult when you are in trouble.

segments.src: ## 今後の注目点
segments.tr: ## Points to watch in the future

segments.src: - 分野別の受け入れ上限の具体的な数字と、その見直しの頻度
segments.tr: - Specific numbers for acceptance caps by sector and the frequency of their review

segments.src: - 転籍が可能になるまでの就労期間や、試験水準の詳細
segments.tr: - Details on the employment period until a transfer becomes possible and the level of examinations

segments.src: - 送出国との二国間取決めの進み具合
segments.tr: - Progress of bilateral agreements with sending countries

segments.src: - 技能実習から育成就労への移行期における、実務上の運用
segments.tr: - Practical operations during the transition period from Technical Intern Training to Training and Employment

segments.src: 人手不足が続くなか、外国人材は日本の産業と地域社会を支える大切な存在です。新制度は、受け入れる側と働く側の双方が対等な関係で信頼を築けるかが問われる仕組みともいえます。開始までの期間を使い、公式情報を確認しながら、無理のない準備を進めていきましょう。
segments.tr: As labor shortages continue, foreign talent is an important presence supporting Japan's industries and local communities. It can be said that the new system is a framework that asks whether both the accepting side and the working side can build trust in an equal relationship. Let's use the time until the start to proceed with preparations without strain while checking official information.

segments.src: > 本記事は一般的な情報提供を目的としており、個別の法的判断や手続きについての助言ではありません。具体的な対応は、所管官庁の公表資料や、行政書士・社会保険労務士などの専門家にご確認ください。
segments.tr: > This article is intended for general information purposes and is not advice on individual legal judgments or procedures. For specific responses, please check the materials published by the competent authorities or consult with experts such as administrative scriveners or labor and social security attorneys.

jp-20261028-news-2.title: Compilation of FY2027 Budget Enters Full Swing: Overview Requests, Defense Spending, Social Security, and Perspectives on "Tax Revenue Growth"

segments.src: 2027年度予算の編成作業が、年末の政府案決定に向けて本格化しています。各省庁の概算要求は高い水準が続いており、歳出の膨張をどう抑え、財源をどう確保するかが大きな論点です。本稿では、予算編成の仕組みと主な数字の見方を整理し、暮らしに関わる見どころを解説します。
segments.tr: The work to compile the FY2027 budget is entering full swing toward the decision on the government draft at the end of the year. Budget requests from various ministries remain at a high level, and how to curb the expansion of expenditures and secure financial resources are major issues. This article organizes the budget compilation mechanism and how to view key figures, and explains highlights related to daily life.

segments.src: > 本稿は一般的な情報提供を目的としています。個別の金額や最新の決定内容は、財務省や各省庁の公表資料でご確認ください。
segments.tr: > This article is intended for general informational purposes. Please check the Ministry of Finance and individual ministry publication materials for specific amounts and the latest decisions.

segments.src: ## 予算編成の流れをおさらい
国の予算は、おおむね次のような順序で固まります。
segments.tr: The national budget is generally finalized in the following order:

segments.src: 1. **夏ごろ**：政府が概算要求の基準（要求の上限の考え方）を示す
segments.tr: 1. **Around Summer**: The government presents the standards for budget requests (the concept of the request ceiling)

segments.src: 2. **8月末まで**：各省庁が翌年度に必要な経費を財務省に提出する（概算要求）
segments.tr: 2. **Until the End of August**: Each ministry submits necessary expenses for the following fiscal year to the Ministry of Finance (budget request)

segments.src: 3. **秋から年末**：財務省が内容を査定し、与党との調整を経て政府案を決める
segments.tr: 3. **From Autumn to Year-End**: The Ministry of Finance assesses the contents and, through adjustments with the ruling party, decides the government draft

segments.src: 4. **年明け以降**：閣議決定後、国会で審議・成立を目指す
segments.tr: 4. **After the New Year**: Following cabinet approval, aiming for deliberation and passage in the Diet

segments.src: 概算要求は「各省庁の希望額」であり、そのまま認められるわけではありません。ただし近年は、社会保障や防衛など増加が見込まれる分野が多く、要求段階から総額が大きくなる傾向があります。
segments.tr: Budget requests are "desired amounts by each ministry" and are not necessarily approved as requested. However, in recent years, there are many fields expected to increase, such as social security and defense, and the total amount tends to be large from the request stage.

segments.src: ## 膨らむ歳出：3つの大きな柱
### 1. 社会保障費
高齢化に伴い、年金・医療・介護の給付費は自然に増えていきます。一般会計の歳出の中でも最大の項目で、近年は30兆円台後半の規模が続いています。診療報酬や介護報酬の改定、物価や賃金の上昇への対応も、増額要因になりやすい点です。
segments.tr: With an aging population, benefit costs for pensions, medical care, and nursing care naturally increase. It is the largest item among general account expenditures, and has continued at a scale in the latter half of the 30 trillion yen range in recent years. Revisions to medical and nursing care fees, as well as responses to rising prices and wages, also tend to be factors for increases.

segments.src: 政府は防衛力の抜本的な強化を進めており、防衛関連の経費は年々増える方向にあります。装備の取得や維持整備、人材確保など中身は多岐にわたり、複数年度にわたる契約の影響も受けます。財源をどう手当てするかが、編成の過程で繰り返し議論されています。
segments.tr: The government is proceeding with a fundamental strengthening of defense capabilities, and defense-related expenses tend to increase year by year. The contents range widely, including equipment procurement, maintenance, and human resource securing, and are also affected by contracts spanning multiple years. How to secure financial resources is repeatedly discussed during the compilation process.

segments.src: 過去に発行した国債の元本返済と利払いにあてる経費です。金利が上昇する局面では、利払い費が膨らみやすくなります。国債残高が大きい日本では、わずかな金利上昇でも負担が積み上がるため、予算の硬直化を招く要因として注目されています。
segments.tr: These are expenses allocated for the principal repayment and interest payments of government bonds issued in the past. In phases of rising interest rates, interest payment costs tend to expand. In Japan, where the government bond balance is large, even a slight increase in interest rates accumulates burdens, drawing attention as a factor causing budget rigidity.

segments.src: ## 「税収増」はどこまで頼れるのか
segments.tr: ## How Much Can We Rely on "Tax Revenue Growth"?

segments.src: 物価上昇や企業収益の改善を背景に、近年の税収は過去最高水準を更新してきました。補正予算の財源に回されたり、予算の見積もりより税収が上振れしたりする場面も目立ちます。
segments.tr: Against the backdrop of rising prices and improving corporate earnings, tax revenues in recent years have updated record highs. Cases where they are diverted to supplementary budget resources or where tax revenues exceed budget estimates are also noticeable.

segments.src: ただし、税収増を前提に歳出を拡大することには注意が必要です。
segments.tr: However, caution is required in expanding expenditures based on the premise of tax revenue growth.

segments.src: - **一時的な要因が含まれる**：物価上昇による消費税収の増加や、企業業績の好調による法人税収は、景気や為替の動向で変わります。
segments.tr: - **Temporary factors are included**: The increase in consumption tax revenue due to price rises and corporate tax revenue due to favorable corporate performance change with economic and exchange rate trends.

segments.src: - **歳出の増え方も大きい**：税収が伸びても、社会保障費や国債費の増加がそれを上回れば、財政の改善にはつながりません。
segments.tr: - **The increase in expenditures is also large**: Even if tax revenues grow, if the increase in social security and government bond expenses exceeds it, it will not lead to fiscal improvement.

segments.src: - **基礎的財政収支の見通し**：政府は財政健全化の目標を掲げていますが、金利上昇の局面では達成の難しさも指摘されています。
segments.tr: - **Primary balance outlook**: The government has set fiscal consolidation goals, but the difficulty of achieving them in phases of rising interest rates has also been pointed out.

segments.src: - **構造的な収支の確認が重要**：税収の上振れ分と、恒常的に増える歳出を分けて見る視点が欠かせません。
segments.tr: - **Confirmation of structural balance is important**: A perspective that separates the upward deviation of tax revenue and constantly increasing expenditures is indispensable.

segments.src: つまり、税収増は追い風ではあるものの、継続的に増える支出の財源として当然に見込めるものではない、という見方が現実的です。
segments.tr: In other words, while tax revenue growth is a tailwind, a realistic view is that it cannot be naturally expected as a financial resource for continuously increasing expenditures.

segments.src: ## 暮らしへの影響：チェックしたいポイント
segments.tr: ## Impact on Daily Life: Points to Check

segments.src: 予算の議論は大きな数字が並びますが、私たちの生活とも結びついています。
segments.tr: Budget discussions line up large numbers, but they are also tied to our lives.

segments.src: - **医療・介護の保険料や自己負担**：給付と負担のバランスの見直しが議論される可能性があります。
segments.tr: - **Medical and nursing care insurance premiums and out-of-pocket costs**: Revisions to the balance between benefits and burdens may be discussed.

segments.src: - **子育て・教育関連の支援策**：継続や拡充の有無、財源の説明に注目が集まります。
segments.tr: - **Childcare and education-related support measures**: Attention gathers on the presence or absence of continuation or expansion, and explanations of financial resources.

segments.src: - **物価・賃上げ対策**：エネルギー価格への支援や、中小企業の価格転嫁を後押しする施策の扱いが焦点です。
segments.tr: - **Price and wage hike measures**: Support for energy prices and the treatment of measures to support price pass-through by small and medium-sized enterprises are focal points.

segments.src: - **税制改正との関係**：予算と同時期に与党税制調査会で議論される税制改正大綱は、家計や企業の負担に直結します。
segments.tr: - **Relationship with tax system reforms**: The tax system reform outline discussed in the ruling party's Tax System Research Commission around the same time as the budget directly links to household and corporate burdens.

segments.src: - **国債の発行額**：新規国債の発行規模は、将来世代の負担や金利動向にも関わります。
segments.tr: - **Government bond issuance amount**: The scale of new government bond issuance is also related to the burden on future generations and interest rate trends.

segments.src: ## 今後の見通しと見方のコツ
segments.tr: ## Future Outlook and Tips for Viewing

segments.src: 年末にかけては、財務省の査定や与党内の調整を通じて、要求の一部が削られたり、別の枠で手当てされたりします。ニュースに接する際は、次の点を意識すると全体像をつかみやすくなります。
segments.tr: Toward the end of the year, through the Ministry of Finance's assessments and adjustments within the ruling party, some requests are cut or covered by other frameworks. When encountering news, keeping the following points in mind makes it easier to grasp the overall picture.

segments.src: 1. **総額だけでなく内訳を見る**：社会保障・防衛・国債費など、増加の中心がどこにあるかを確認する。
segments.tr: 1. **Look at the breakdown, not just the total**: Check where the center of increase is, such as social security, defense, and government bond expenses.

segments.src: 2. **前提となる経済見通しを確認する**：成長率、物価、金利の想定が変わると、税収や国債費の数字も変わる。
segments.tr: 2. **Check the underlying economic outlook**: If assumptions for growth rates, prices, and interest rates change, the figures for tax revenue and government bond expenses also change.

segments.src: 3. **「当初予算」と「補正予算」を分けて考える**：実際の財政負担は、補正予算を含めた総額で見る必要がある。
segments.tr: "Initial budget" and "supplementary budget" must be considered separately: Actual fiscal burden needs to be viewed in total including the supplementary budget.

segments.src: 4. **財源の説明に注目する**：税収、国債、その他収入のうち、何でまかなうのかが明示されているかを確かめる。
segments.tr: 4. **Pay attention to explanations of financial resources**: Verify whether it is clearly stated what will cover the costs among tax revenue, government bonds, and other income.

segments.src: ## まとめ
2027年度予算の編成では、社会保障費・防衛費・国債費という「増えやすい支出」と、税収の上振れという「不確実な収入」のバランスが問われます。税収増は心強い材料ですが、それだけに頼らず、歳出の中身と財源の説明を丁寧に見ていくことが大切です。今後の政府案の公表や国会審議に向けて、公的な資料や報道を比較しながら動向を追っていきましょう。
segments.tr: In the compilation of the FY2027 budget, the balance between "expenditures that tend to increase"—social security, defense, and government bonds—and "uncertain income"—upward deviations in tax revenue—is questioned. While tax revenue growth is an encouraging material, it is important not to rely solely on it, but to carefully examine the contents of expenditures and explanations of financial resources. Let's follow trends while comparing official materials and reports toward the future publication of the government draft and Diet deliberations.

jp-20261028-international-logistics-tran.title: [International Logistics & Transport #6] Is it better to “lease” a ship than to “buy” one? The 3 types of charter contracts and how demurrage works

segments.src: > 船を借りる方法は「1航海だけ」「期間で」「船体だけ」の3通り。誰が何のコストとリスクを負うかが、契約の違いのすべてです。
segments.tr: > There are three ways to hire a ship: “for a single voyage,” “for a period of time,” and “bareboat.” The difference between the contracts comes down entirely to who bears which costs and risks.

segments.src: ## 今日の概念
鉄鉱石や石炭、穀物を大量に運びたい会社が、必ず自社で船を持っているとは限りません。むしろ多くの場合、船主（船を所有する会社）から船を借りて運びます。この「船を借りる契約」が用船契約（チャーター契約）です。「傭船」と書かれることもあります。
segments.tr: Companies that need to move large quantities of iron ore, coal, or grain do not necessarily own their own ships. More often than not, they hire ships from shipowners (companies that own vessels) and transport cargo with them. This ship-hiring contract is a charter party (charter contract). It is sometimes written as 傭船 (yōsen).

segments.src: 用船契約は大きく3つに分かれます。違いを見分けるポイントは、**「船を動かす責任（船員・運航）」と「費用（燃料・港の費用など）」を誰が持つか**です。
segments.tr: Charter contracts fall into three broad categories. The key to telling them apart is **who bears responsibility for operating the ship (crew and operations) and who bears the costs (fuel, port charges, etc.)**.

segments.src: 航海用船（ボヤージ・チャーター）**
「A港からB港まで、この貨物を1回運んでください」という契約です。料金は主に「貨物1トンあたりいくら」という**運賃**で決まります。船員の手配も燃料代も、基本的には船主側が負担します。借り手（用船者）は、貨物を用意して約束どおりに積み降ろしすれば済みます。タクシーで「目的地まで」と頼むイメージに近い契約です。
segments.tr: This is a contract in which you say, “Please carry this cargo once from Port A to Port B.” The fee is mainly determined by the **freight rate**, “so much per ton of cargo.” The shipowner basically bears the cost of arranging the crew as well as the fuel. The charterer only needs to prepare the cargo and load and unload it as agreed. It is close to asking a taxi to “take me to this destination.”

segments.src: 定期用船（タイム・チャーター）**
「この船を6か月（または数年）借ります」という、期間で借りる契約です。料金は「1日あたりいくら」という用船料（ハイヤー）です。船員の配乗や船の保守は船主が引き続き担いますが、どの港へ行くか・何を運ぶかは用船者が決め、**燃料費や港費は用船者の負担**になるのが一般的です。運転手付きのレンタカーを期間契約し、ガソリン代と行き先はこちら持ち、という感覚です。
segments.tr: This is a contract for a period of time: “We will hire this ship for six months (or several years).” The fee is the hire rate (charter hire), “so much per day.” The shipowner continues to handle crew assignment and ship maintenance, but the charterer decides which ports to visit and what to carry, and it is common for the **charterer to bear the fuel and port costs**. It is like renting a car with a driver for a set term, where you pay for the gasoline and choose the destinations.

segments.src: 裸用船（ベアボート・チャーター）**
船体だけを借りる契約です。船員の手配も、保守・保険・運航も、原則として**すべて用船者側**が引き受けます。実質的には「自社船のように使う」形で、運転手なしのリース車に近いイメージです。
segments.tr: This is a contract to hire only the hull of the ship. In principle, the charterer takes on **all** responsibility for arranging the crew as well as maintenance, insurance, and operation. In effect, the ship is used “as if it were the company's own,” which is similar to leasing a car without a driver.

segments.src: まとめると、航海用船 → 定期用船 → 裸用船の順に、用船者が負う責任と自由度が大きくなっていきます。
segments.tr: To sum up, moving from voyage charter to time charter to bareboat charter, the responsibility and degree of freedom borne by the charterer increase in that order.

segments.src: ### 時間はお金：滞船料と早出料
segments.tr: ### Time Is Money: Demurrage and Despatch

segments.src: 航海用船で特に重要なのが「時間」の取り決めです。契約では、港で荷物を積み降ろしするために使ってよい期間（**停泊期間、レイタイム**）を決めておきます。
segments.tr: The most important point in a voyage charter is the arrangement regarding **time**. The contract sets the period the ship may stay in port for loading and discharging cargo (**laytime**).

segments.src: - 用船者側の事情でこの期間を超えると、超過した日数に応じて滞船料（デマレージ）を船主に支払います。船主にとって、船が港で止まっている時間は次の仕事に使えない「損失」だからです。
segments.tr: - If, due to circumstances on the charterer's side, this period is exceeded, the charterer pays the shipowner **demurrage** according to the number of excess days. This is because, for the shipowner, time a ship sits idle in port is a “loss,” since the ship cannot be used for its next job.

segments.src: - 逆に、期間より早く終われば、船主から早出料（デスパッチ）が支払われる契約もあります。
segments.tr: - Conversely, if the operation finishes earlier than the allowed period, some contracts provide that the shipowner pays **despatch money**.

segments.src: 滞船料は1日あたりの金額で決められることが多く、港の混雑や悪天候、貨物の準備遅れで思わぬ出費になることがあります。どんな事情を停泊期間に数えるか（例えば休日や荒天を除くかどうか）も、契約文言で細かく定められます。
segments.tr: Demurrage is often set as a daily amount, and congestion at the port, bad weather, or delays in preparing the cargo can lead to unexpected expenses. The specifics of which circumstances count toward laytime (for example, whether holidays or stormy weather are excluded) are also set out in detail in the contract wording.

segments.src: ## 日常の中で
ある日本の鉄鋼メーカーが、オーストラリア西部から日本の製鉄所へ鉄鉱石を運ぶ場面を考えてみましょう（数字はすべて説明用の仮のものです）。
segments.tr: Consider a scene in which a Japanese steel manufacturer ships iron ore from western Australia to its steelworks in Japan (all figures are hypothetical, for illustration).

segments.src: - **スポットで1回だけ運びたい** → 航海用船。「1トンあたり○ドル」で契約し、船の運航は船主任せ。
segments.tr: - **Want to ship once on a spot basis** → Voyage charter. Contract at “$○ per ton,” with ship operation left to the shipowner.

segments.src: - **今後1年、毎月のように運ぶ** → 定期用船。1日あたりの用船料を払って船を確保し、燃料の手配や配船スケジュールは自社（またはグループの海運会社）で管理。
segments.tr: - **Shipping roughly every month over the next year** → Time charter. Pay a daily hire rate to secure the ship, and the company (or its group shipping company) manages fuel arrangements and the sailing schedule.

segments.src: 航海用船で、停泊期間を「3日」と決めていたとします。ところが日本側の港で岸壁が混み合い、荷揚げ完了までに5日かかりました。滞船料が仮に1日2万ドル（1ドル150円換算で約300万円）なら、超過2日分で約600万円の追加負担になります。
segments.tr: Suppose that under a voyage charter, the laytime was set at “3 days.” However, the berth at the Japanese port was congested, and it took 5 days to finish unloading. If demurrage is, say, $20,000 per day (about ¥3 million at ¥150 to the dollar), the 2 extra days would add roughly ¥6 million in additional costs.

segments.src: この会社の物流担当者にとっては、「運賃が安いか」だけでなく、「港で待たされたら誰が払うのか」「停泊期間に何を含めるのか」まで読み込むことが、コスト管理の大事な仕事になるわけです。
segments.tr: For the logistics staff at this company, managing costs means reading closely not just whether the freight rate is cheap, but also “who pays if the ship is kept waiting at port” and “what is included in laytime.”

segments.src: ## 3行まとめ
1. 用船契約には、1航海単位の**航海用船**、期間単位の**定期用船**、船体だけを借りる**裸用船**がある。
segments.tr: 1. Charter contracts include the **voyage charter**, which is per voyage; the **time charter**, which is per period; and the **bareboat charter**, which covers only the hull.

segments.src: 2. 違いの本質は、船員・運航・燃料などの**責任と費用を誰が負うか**。裸用船ほど用船者の負担と自由度が大きい。
segments.tr: 2. The essence of the difference is **who bears responsibility and costs** for crew, operations, and fuel. The more bareboat-like the contract, the greater the charterer's burden and freedom.

segments.src: 3. 航海用船では停泊期間を超えると**滞船料**が発生し、早く終われば**早出料**がもらえることもある。
segments.tr: 3. In a voyage charter, if laytime is exceeded, **demurrage** is incurred; if the operation finishes early, the charterer may receive **despatch money**.

segments.src: ## ✅ セルフクイズ
**Q1.** 「1日あたりの用船料」を払って一定期間船を借り、燃料費は借り手が負担するのが一般的な契約はどれ？
segments.tr: **Q1.** Which contract is one in which a party pays a **daily hire rate** to rent a ship for a set period, with the charterer generally bearing the fuel costs?

segments.src: - A. 航海用船
- B. 定期用船
- C. 裸用船
**Q2.** 【O/X】裸用船では、船員の手配は原則として船主が行う。
segments.tr: **Q2.** 【True/False】 In a bareboat charter, the shipowner in principle arranges the crew.

segments.src: **Q3.** 航海用船で、合意した停泊期間を用船者側の事情で超えた場合に船主へ支払うものは？
segments.tr: **Q3.** In a voyage charter, what is paid to the shipowner when the agreed laytime is exceeded due to circumstances on the charterer's side?

segments.src: - A. 早出料
- B. 運賃
- C. 滞船料
## 📚 今日の用語
- **用船契約（チャーター）**：船主から船を借りて貨物輸送に使うための契約。
segments.tr: - **Charter party (charter)**: A contract for hiring a ship from its owner to carry cargo.

segments.src: - **航海用船**：特定の航海1回（または数回）単位で船を借りる契約。主に貨物量に応じた運賃で支払う。
segments.tr: - **Voyage charter**: A contract to hire a ship for one voyage (or a few voyages), usually paid by freight according to cargo volume.

segments.src: - **定期用船**：一定期間単位で船を借りる契約。1日あたりの用船料を支払い、運航指示は用船者が出す。
segments.tr: - **Time charter**: A contract to hire a ship for a set period. The charterer pays a daily hire rate and issues the operating instructions.

segments.src: - **裸用船**：船体のみを借り、船員・保守・運航を用船者が担う契約。
segments.tr: - **Bareboat charter**: A contract to hire only the hull, with the charterer responsible for crew, maintenance, and operations.

segments.src: - **滞船料（デマレージ）／早出料（デスパッチ）**：停泊期間を超過したときに用船者が払う補償金／期間内に早く終えたときに船主が払う報奨金。
segments.tr: - **Demurrage / Despatch**: Demurrage is compensation paid by the charterer when laytime is exceeded. Despatch money is a bonus paid by the shipowner when the operation is finished early within the allowed time.

segments.src: *正解：Q1 = B（定期用船は期間で借り、用船料は日額。燃料費・港費は用船者負担が一般的）／Q2 = X（裸用船では船員の手配も用船者側が行うのが原則）／Q3 = C（滞船料。早出料は逆に、早く終えたときに船主から支払われるもの）*
segments.tr: *Answers: Q1 = B (Time charter: hired for a period at a daily hire rate; the charterer generally bears fuel and port costs) / Q2 = X (In a bareboat charter, the charterer in principle also arranges the crew) / Q3 = C (Demurrage. Despatch money is the reverse: paid by the shipowner when the operation finishes early)*

jp-20261028-news-3.title: Gold prices remain at historical highs: The background behind 'safe-haven' popularity, how individuals can invest in gold, and key points to note

segments.src: 金(ゴールド)の価格が歴史的な高値圏で推移しています。ニュースで「金価格が最高値を更新」といった見出しを目にする機会も増え、「今から始めても遅いのでは」「どんな方法があるのか」と関心を持つ人が多くなっています。この記事では、金が注目される背景、円建て価格の見方、個人が利用できる主な投資手段、そして値動きとの付き合い方を、できるだけやさしく整理します。
segments.tr: Gold prices are currently hovering at historical highs. With an increasing number of headlines in the news reporting that "gold prices have reached record highs," more people are becoming interested, wondering, "Isn't it too late to start now?" or "What kind of methods are available?" This article aims to clearly and simply explain the background behind why gold is gaining attention, how to view yen-denominated prices, the main investment methods available to individuals, and how to navigate price fluctuations.

segments.src: ※本記事は一般的な情報提供を目的としており、特定の商品の購入や売却を勧めるものではありません。投資の最終判断はご自身で行ってください。
segments.tr: *This article is intended for general informational purposes only and does not recommend the purchase or sale of any specific product. Please make your final investment decisions at your own discretion.

segments.src: ## 金が「安全資産」と呼ばれる理由
segments.tr: ## Why gold is called a "safe-haven asset"

segments.src: 金は、株式や債券と違って、企業の業績や発行体の信用に直接左右されない資産です。古くから世界中で価値が認められてきたことから、市場が不安定になったときに資金の逃避先として選ばれやすく、「安全資産」と呼ばれています。
segments.tr: Unlike stocks and bonds, gold is an asset not directly tied to corporate performance or the credit of an issuer. Because its value has been recognized worldwide since ancient times, it tends to be chosen as a safe haven for capital when markets become unstable, which is why it is called a "safe-haven asset."

segments.src: ただし、「安全」といっても価格が下がらないという意味ではありません。あくまで「ほかの資産が不安定なときに相対的に注目されやすい」という性質を表した言葉です。この点は最初に押さえておきたいポイントです。
segments.tr: However, being "safe" does not mean the price will never fall. The term simply describes the property that "it tends to attract relative attention when other assets are unstable." This is a point worth noting from the beginning.

segments.src: ## 高値圏が続く主な背景
segments.tr: ## Main background behind the continued high prices

segments.src: ### 1. 地政学リスクの高まり
紛争や国際関係の緊張など、先行きが見通しにくい出来事が続くと、投資家はリスクを避けようとして金に資金を移す傾向があります。不透明感が強いほど、金への需要が高まりやすくなります。
segments.tr: When unpredictable events such as conflicts or international tensions continue, investors tend to shift funds into gold to avoid risks. The higher the uncertainty, the greater the demand for gold tends to be.

segments.src: ### 2. 各国の中央銀行による買い増し
segments.tr: ### 3. Central bank purchases across various countries

segments.src: 近年、新興国を中心に、中央銀行が外貨準備の一部として金を積み増す動きが目立っています。特定の通貨への依存を減らし、資産を分散する狙いがあるとされます。中央銀行の買いは長期的かつ継続的になりやすく、価格を支える要因の一つと考えられています。
segments.tr: In recent years, particularly in emerging economies, central banks have increasingly accumulated gold as part of their foreign exchange reserves. This is believed to be aimed at reducing dependence on specific currencies and diversifying assets. Central bank purchases tend to be long-term and continuous, which is considered one of the factors supporting prices.

segments.src: ### 3. 金利や為替の見通し
segments.tr: ### 3. Interest rate and exchange rate outlooks

segments.src: 金は利息や配当を生まない資産です。そのため、一般に金利が高いときは相対的に魅力が下がり、金利が低下する局面では魅力が高まりやすいとされます。米国の金利動向や、ドルの強弱も金価格に影響する代表的な要因です。
segments.tr: Gold is an asset that does not generate interest or dividends. Therefore, its relative appeal generally declines when interest rates are high, while its appeal tends to increase during phases of falling interest rates. U.S. interest rate trends and the strength of the dollar are also representative factors influencing gold prices.

segments.src: ## 円建て価格の見方
日本で私たちが目にする金価格は「円建て」です。国際的な金価格はドル建てで取引されるため、円建て価格は次の2つの動きが組み合わさって決まります。
segments.tr: The gold prices we see in Japan are "yen-denominated." Because international gold prices are traded in U.S. dollars, yen-denominated prices are determined by a combination of the following two movements:

segments.src: - ドル建ての金価格(国際相場)
- 為替レート(円とドルの関係)
segments.tr: - Exchange rate (relationship between the yen and the dollar)

segments.src: たとえば、ドル建ての金価格が横ばいでも、円安が進めば円建て価格は上がります。逆に、円高になれば円建ての価格は押し下げられます。円建て価格が高値圏にある背景には、国際価格の上昇に加えて為替の影響があることも多く、両方を分けて見ることが大切です。
segments.tr: For example, even if dollar-denominated gold prices remain flat, yen-denominated prices will rise if the yen depreciates. Conversely, if the yen appreciates, yen-denominated prices are pushed down. The fact that yen-denominated prices are at high levels is often due to exchange rate effects in addition to rising international prices, and it is important to look at both separately.

segments.src: ## 個人が金に投資する主な方法
segments.tr: ## Main ways for individuals to invest in gold

segments.src: ### 現物(地金・金貨)
金の延べ棒やコインを実際に購入する方法です。手元に実物が残る安心感がある一方、次のような点に注意が必要です。
segments.tr: This is the method of actually purchasing gold bars or coins. While there is a sense of security in having the physical object at hand, the following points require attention:

segments.src: - 売値と買値に差があり、手数料や加工費がかかる場合がある
segments.tr: - There is a difference between selling and buying prices, and commissions or processing fees may apply

segments.src: - 保管場所や盗難・紛失への備えが必要
segments.tr: - Storage locations and preparations against theft or loss are necessary

segments.src: - 売却時に本人確認書類や領収書などが求められることがある
segments.tr: - Personal identification documents or receipts may be required upon sale

segments.src: ### 純金積立
毎月一定額を自動で買い付けていく方法で、数千円程度から始められる商品もあります。購入タイミングを分散できるため、高値圏で一度に買ってしまうリスクを抑えやすいのが特徴です。ただし、手数料や、売却・受け取り時の費用は事業者によって異なるため、事前に確認しましょう。
segments.tr: This is a method of automatically purchasing a fixed amount every month, with some products starting from around several thousand yen. Since purchase timing can be spread out, it is easy to suppress the risk of buying all at once at high prices. However, since fees and costs at the time of sale or receipt vary by provider, be sure to check in advance.

segments.src: ### 金ETF・金に連動する投資信託
segments.tr: ### Gold ETFs and gold-linked investment trusts

segments.src: 証券口座を通じて、金価格に連動する商品を株式のように売買できます。少額から始めやすく、保管の手間がないのが利点です。一方で、運用コスト(信託報酬など)がかかる点や、為替ヘッジの有無によって値動きが変わる点に注意が必要です。
segments.tr: Through a securities account, you can buy and sell products linked to gold prices just like stocks. The advantages are that it is easy to start with small amounts and there is no hassle of storage. On the other hand, attention must be paid to operational costs (such as trust fees) and the fact that price movements change depending on the presence or absence of currency hedging.

segments.src: ### 金関連の株式や先物など
金鉱会社の株式や先物取引といった方法もありますが、値動きが大きくなりやすく、仕組みも複雑です。初心者の方は、まず基本的な手段から理解するのがおすすめです。
segments.tr: Methods such as gold mining company stocks and futures trading also exist, but price movements tend to be large and the mechanisms are complex. Beginners are recommended to start by understanding basic methods first.

segments.src: ## 手段ごとの違いのまとめ
| 方法 | 始めやすさ | 保管の手間 | 主な注意点 |

segments.tr: | Physical | Moderately high | Required | Trading price gap, storage |

segments.src: ## 値動きの大きさとの付き合い方
segments.tr: ## How to deal with the magnitude of price fluctuations

segments.src: 金は「安定している」というイメージを持たれがちですが、実際には短期間で大きく上下することがあります。高値圏にあるときは、とくに調整(価格の下落)が起こる可能性も意識しておく必要があります。
segments.tr: Gold tends to have the image of being "stable," but in reality, it can fluctuate significantly in a short period. When prices are at high levels, it is especially necessary to be aware of the possibility that adjustments (price drops) may occur.

segments.src: - **一度に買わず、時間を分散する**:積立のように、購入時期をずらすと平均的な取得価格がならされやすくなります。
segments.tr: - **Do not buy all at once, spread out time**: Like accumulation plans, shifting purchase timing makes the average acquisition price easier to smooth out.

segments.src: - **資産全体の中の割合を決める**:金に偏らず、株式や預貯金などとのバランスを考えましょう。一般に、資産の一部にとどめる考え方が広く紹介されています。
segments.tr: - **Decide the proportion within your overall assets**: Avoid concentrating solely on gold and consider a balance with stocks, savings, etc. Generally, the idea of keeping it as a part of one's assets is widely introduced.

segments.src: - **余裕資金で行う**:生活費や近い将来に使う予定のお金は、投資に回さないのが基本です。
segments.tr: - **Use surplus funds**: The basic rule is not to allocate living expenses or money scheduled to be used in the near future to investments.

segments.src: - **長期の視点を持つ**:日々の値動きに一喜一憂せず、自分の目的や期間に合った運用を心がけましょう。
segments.tr: - **Have a long-term perspective**: Try not to be swayed by daily price movements and aim for management that suits your own purpose and timeframe.

segments.src: - **税金とコストを確認する**:売却益には税金がかかる場合があり、商品によって扱いが異なります。詳細は税務署や専門家に確認してください。
segments.tr: - **Check taxes and costs**: Capital gains may be subject to tax, and treatment varies depending on the product. Please check with tax offices or experts for details.

segments.src: ## 注意したいポイント
- 「必ず儲かる」「今すぐ買わないと損をする」といった勧誘には慎重になりましょう。
segments.tr: - Be cautious of solicitations such as "you will definitely make a profit" or "you will lose out if you don't buy now."

segments.src: - 過去の値上がりは、将来の値上がりを保証するものではありません。
segments.tr: - Past price increases do not guarantee future price increases.

segments.src: - 金は利息や配当を生まないため、価格の変動が収益のほぼすべてになります。
segments.tr: - Because gold does not generate interest or dividends, price fluctuations account for almost all returns.

segments.src: - 取扱事業者が金融庁などに登録されているか、手数料体系が明確かを確認しましょう。
segments.tr: - Check whether the handling business operator is registered with the Financial Services Agency and whether the fee structure is clear.

segments.src: ## まとめ
金価格が高値圏にある背景には、地政学リスク、中央銀行の買い増し、金利や為替の動きなど、複数の要因が重なっています。個人が金に投資する方法には、現物、純金積立、ETFなどがあり、それぞれコストや手間、リスクが異なります。高値圏だからこそ、一度に大きく投資するのではなく、無理のない金額で分散しながら、自分の目的に合った方法を選ぶことが大切です。
segments.tr: The background behind gold prices being at high levels involves a combination of multiple factors, such as geopolitical risks, central bank purchases, and interest rate and exchange rate movements. Methods for individuals to invest in gold include physical gold, accumulation plans, and ETFs, each with different costs, effort, and risks. Precisely because prices are high, rather than making large investments all at once, it is important to diversify with reasonable amounts and choose a method that suits your purpose.

segments.src: 情報を集めるときは、公的機関や信頼できる金融機関の資料も参考にし、納得したうえで判断しましょう。
segments.tr: When gathering information, also refer to materials from public institutions and reliable financial institutions, and make decisions after fully understanding them.
